precepts.text: Shemaiah counseled Nehemiah to hide in the temple because they will come to slay thee; Nehemiah answered, Should such a man as I flee? He was the governor the Most High set up for everybody to look up to, and he would not go in.
precepts.point: Nehemiah shows the right spirit. In the Persian captivity he had liberty from the king to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, and the enemies Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem plotted to scare him off the work. A hired man urged him to hide in the temple because they were coming to slay him, and Nehemiah refused; operating in the spirit of fear is sin according to the scripture.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
The Philistines came up with “thirty thousand chariots, and six thousand horsemen, and people as the sand which is on the sea shore in multitude”, far deeper than the three thousand Israel had prepared. The men of Israel saw they were in a strait and hid themselves “in caves, and in thickets, and in rocks, and in high places, and in pits.” The sons of God, the mighty men of valor, saw the enemy coming and started hiding, though the Lord had just defeated the Philistines for Israel in chapter 7.

Nehemiah shows the right spirit. In the Persian captivity he had liberty from the king to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, and the enemies Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem plotted to scare him off the work. Shemaiah counseled him to hide: “Let us meet together in the house of God, within the temple, and let us shut the doors of the temple: for they will come to slay thee; yea, in the night will they come to slay thee.”

Nehemiah answered, “Should such a man as I flee? and who is there, that, being as I am, would go into the temple to save his life? I will not go in.” He was the governor the Most High set up for everybody to look up to, and he would not go in.

precepts.text: Nehemiah perceived that God had not sent him, but that Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him, that he should be afraid, and do so, and sin, and that they might have matter for an evil report to reproach him; fear in the leader would let the enemy call him weak and unfit to lead.

A hired man urged him to hide in the temple because they were coming to slay him, and Nehemiah refused; operating in the spirit of fear is sin according to the scripture.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
Nehemiah saw through it: “And, lo, I perceived that God had not sent him; but that he pronounced this prophecy against me: for Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.” And he names the purpose: “Therefore was he hired, that I should be afraid, and do so, and sin, and that they might have matter for an evil report, that they might reproach me.”

Afraid, and do so, and sin: operating in the spirit of fear is sin according to the scripture. Fear in the leader would let the enemy call him weak and unfit to lead. Israel did what Nehemiah refused to do; they hid, and the people that stayed with Saul “followed him trembling.”

precepts.text: The Lord did not give us the spirit of fear; for the people of the Most High, fearfulness before the enemy is unbelief.

precepts.why:
“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” The Lord did not give us the spirit of fear.

As the chosen people, if we really have faith we should be fearless. For the people of the Most High, fearfulness before the enemy is unbelief. The Lord had just defeated the Philistines for Israel; to still fear the enemy shows a lack of faith, that you really do not believe in your God.

precepts.text: Saul made haste in a time of trouble; he panicked and did unadvisedly, and he is going to suffer consequences for it.
precepts.point: Brothers do the same thing today: leadership said it would be here at ten, it is five past ten, so we cancel the plan and go home. Be humble and tarry like you were instructed; it may run some minutes over, and the Lord may be testing your patience.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
Samuel had instructed Saul in chapter 10: when you get to Gilgal, tarry seven days, make no moves until I arrive. Saul “tarried seven days, according to the set time that Samuel had appointed: but Samuel came not to Gilgal; and the people were scattered from him.” The people were acting frantic, and Saul said, “Bring hither a burnt offering to me, and peace offerings. And he offered the burnt offering.” Saul is not the priest; that is Samuel’s office.

“Set thy heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.” Saul made haste in a time of trouble. He panicked and did unadvisedly, and he is going to suffer consequences for it. Then, “as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came”: he was barely late, and Saul could not hold his patience.

Brothers do the same thing today: leadership said it would be here at ten, it is five past ten, so we cancel the plan and go home. Be humble and tarry like you were instructed. It may run some minutes over, and the Lord may be testing your patience.

precepts.text: Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer, if thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke and the putting forth of the finger; the Most High says stop playing the blame game if you want him to intervene on your behalf, but pointing the finger is exactly what Saul did.
precepts.point: Samuel asks, What hast thou done? Saul answers with excuses: the people were scattered from me, thou camest not within the days appointed, the Philistines gathered at Michmash, so I forced myself and offered a burnt offering. This is part of Saul's pattern of behavior; he never wants to hold himself accountable, he always deflects onto whoever else.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
Samuel asks, “What hast thou done?” and Saul answers with excuses: “Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and that thou camest not within the days appointed, and that the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash”, so “I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering.” This is part of Saul’s pattern of behavior: he never wants to hold himself accountable; he always deflects onto whoever else.

“Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity”. The Most High says stop playing the blame game if you want him to intervene on your behalf. Pointing the finger is exactly what Saul did.

precepts.text: Abraham drew down with the knife even when it made no fleshly sense, and Joseph, betrayed and tempted, kept the commandment in the time of his distress and was exalted to be lord of Egypt; loyalty to the Lord regardless of circumstances is what the trial is for.
precepts.point: The Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart to be captain over his people. Samuel prophesied this without ever having met the replacement; that man is David, predestined before he is even introduced in the scriptures.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
Samuel does not entertain the excuses: “Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the Lord thy God, which he commanded thee”. Saul thought he was only bending Samuel’s word, but disobeying the instruction was disobeying the commandment of the Lord. For that one act of foolishness the Lord withdrew what he would have given, Saul’s lineage ruling Israel: “for now would the Lord have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever. But now thy kingdom shall not continue”.

The Lord wants to see whether you will perform what he told you to do even when things do not work out how you planned. “Was not Abraham found faithful in temptation, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness?” Abraham drew down with the knife even when it made no fleshly sense. “Joseph in the time of his distress kept the commandment and was made lord of Egypt.” Joseph was betrayed and tempted, kept the commandment, and was exalted.

Loyalty to the Lord regardless of circumstances is what the trial is for. That is what proves you faithful in temptation and worthy of being exalted, and Saul failed that test in the time of his distress.

precepts.text: When he had removed Saul, he raised up unto them David to be their king: I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.
precepts.point: The Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart to be captain over his people. Samuel prophesied this without ever having met the replacement; that man is David, predestined before he is even introduced in the scriptures.

note.label: 1 Samuel 13: Make Not Haste in Time of Trouble

precepts.why:
Samuel told Saul, “the Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the Lord hath commanded him to be captain over his people”. Samuel prophesied this without ever having met the replacement.

Paul names him: “And when he had removed him, he raised up unto them David to be their king; to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.” That man is David, predestined before he is even introduced in the scriptures. Saul had not kept that which the Lord commanded; David was the one which shall fulfil all his will.

moments.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: This is Samuel speaking to Saul. But now thy kingdom shall not continue: because of disobedience. Remember what he told him to do with Amalek; he refused. He was supposed to slay the whole city of Amalek, and he spared Agag and some of the flocks. God said, no, you're walking in disobedience. Therefore I'm going to replace you. You are going to become obsolete. I'm going to replace you with something greater than yourself to fulfill God's purpose.
And guess what? The house of Saul is back here today. We see them on social media. You got the house of David and you got the house of Saul back here today. No new thing under the sun.
Because thou hast not kept that which the Lord commanded thee: you're not keeping his laws. You're defiling doctrine, coming up with your new understanding.
